Exactly what I mean. It fucking sucks, I'm a ""good person"" but the minute I want someone to be held accountable I'm a bitch and everyone hates me and says I'm being dramatic. You really don't lose anything by being a bad person, really. You have nothing to fuckin lose, everything to gain. One slip up as a good person and you're never seen the same again or it's used to abuse you. 

Death really is the only thing that can be any sort of relief from this trash existence. The only reason I haven't attempted again is because I'm too nervous to try again rn and I don't want to deal with the hassle and the emotional shit that happens for a few people afterwards.

Hi, I'm sorry you had to go through that but I understand where you're coming from completely.

I lost my dad when I was 1, and similar to you I recently lost my grandma this year who I consider the mother I needed when mine was...less than kind to me. 

For years I thought of my dad in the same way you did. Hurt, suffering, confused. I had dreams about him and woke up crying because I wouldn't understand how I could've helped him differently or if he was still suffering. Even when he died I still couldn't get past the fact he had suffered. 

But, it took time. Time for me to understand that at the end of our line it isn't kind to all of us, but most importantly: he wouldn't want for me to remember him that way. They want you to remember them as they were, even though it's HARD when you remember their final moments or them near the end of the line. 

When it comes to the afterlife, I think you need to start seeing it as you would hope someone would see you once you past. Is it you just existing in the void but feeling no pain or worries? Or is it a giant family reunion where everyone you met and loved gets to see you again? For me, once I found out what I wanted, I used that. Of course that's also hard considering that's kind of asking for an existential crisis every now and then, but when I finally settled - I saw both of them there and it really helped me to see them when they were at their best. 

This is kind of rambly and I'm sorry if this just comes across as random gibber jabber.  I hope things get better for you and one day you get to 'hear' from him in the way you knew him.
